judged_text: The computed schema keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the constant string '[object Object]' (zod schemas have no custom toString) and collapse into one duplicate key, so minimumTokenResponseSchema requires only access_token and implements none of the intended expiry or refresh_token validation. In sync mode the schema accepts any response containing an access_token string while zod's default unknown-key stripping silently deletes every other field from the parsed data: office365-calendar keeps a stale expires_in and re-runs the refresh on every single calendar operation (a sync fetch plus a DB write per booking), and salesforce — whose own provider response is run through this branch too, because the branch keys only off the env flags — persists key = {access_token, refresh_token}, losing instance_url so the next operation builds its jsforce connection against an undefined instance URL and every Salesforce call fails, all while parse reports success.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, minimumTokenResponseSchema defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. In JS object literals, those computed keys are evaluated immediately to a string; for Zod schema objects this will be a constant (e.g., "[object Object]"), so the two entries collide and do not create a dynamic “any string key” shape. As a result, in sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) the schema effectively only requires `access_token` and strips all other fields, so token responses can be “successfully” parsed while losing important fields (e.g., Office365 token fields, Salesforce `instance_url`). The subsequent code updates persisted credentials based on this parsed data, making the behavior/data-loss claim grounded in the diff.
